summary: Hitline shows the tracking tags and events of the page you are inspecting. It does not collect, keep or send any data about you or the pages you check.
reads: The network requests, dataLayer and GTM containers of the inspected tab, plus the tracking cookies _ga, _gcl_*, _fbp, _fbc, _ttp and FPID, only while the Hitline tab in Chrome DevTools is open.
The page in the current tab, only after you click the Hitline icon to open the popup.
A tracking plan file, only if you choose to load one. It is read in your browser.
stores: Your settings in Chrome storage on your computer: the language, the domains you list as your own site, and the tracking plans you load (event and parameter names only).
Results stay in the open panel and are gone when you close DevTools or the popup.
never: Read tabs you did not open Hitline on
Read what you type into forms
Send events, pages or results to any server
Keep a history of the sites you checked

perms.name: activeTab
perms.why: Read the current tab, and only after you click the icon.

perms.name: scripting
perms.why: Run the reading function in that tab.

perms.name: storage
perms.why: Save your settings on your computer.

perms.name: devtools_page
perms.why: Add the Hitline tab to DevTools. Chrome gives it the inspected tab’s requests only while DevTools is open.

notes: The audit PDF is made in your browser and saved where you choose.
When you click "Reload page" in the panel, Hitline adds a small script to that page that notes when each dataLayer entry is pushed. It reads nothing else and sends nothing.
Hitline makes no network requests of its own.
